origins.section: One Abstract Method Makes an Interface Functional; @FunctionalInterface Only Checks It
One Abstract Method Makes an Interface Functional; @FunctionalInterface Only Checks It
Use java.util.function Until a Name, a Checked Exception or a Third Parameter Asks for Your Own
Function<Integer, Integer> Boxes Each Value Unless the JIT Removes It; IntUnaryOperator Never Boxes
Accept Function<? super T, ? extends R>, or Callers' Functions Don't Fit

gates.says: all 5 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-object-methods-in-interface: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-object-methods-in-interface: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-object-methods-in-interface: Decided by: 'A lambda can target any interface with exactly one abstract method left once `default` and `static` methods, and abstract redeclarations of `Object`'s public methods, are set aside.' equals and hashCode are Object's public methods, negate is default, so matches is the one left.

recorded.pass:q-unannotated-second-method: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-unannotated-second-method: Decided by: 'Without the annotation `RateLimit.java` still compiles, and the error appears in whichever file holds a lambda' (Gateway.java error 'RateLimit is not a functional interface'). The declaring repo holds no lambda, so no error there; the service builds fail.
recorded.prompt:q-same-shape-interface: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-same-shape-interface: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-same-shape-interface: Decided by: 'Every boundary needs an adapter (`decimal::parse`)' and 'A lambda fits either type'. The page shows the method-reference adapter as the fix; it does not state the general claim 'any functional interface whose method fits', but the adapter usage supports the option.
recorded.prompt:q-boxing-many-steps: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-boxing-many-steps: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-boxing-many-steps: Decided by: 'With three, the call site was megamorphic and was not inlined, so every call allocated two 16-byte `Integer`s ... A shared pipeline that runs many lambdas through one call site is the second case.'
recorded.prompt:q-predicate-invariance: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-predicate-invariance: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-predicate-invariance: Decided by analogy from the Function example: 'inference variable T has incompatible equality constraints Object,Integer' and '`T` must be `Integer` for the list and `Object` for the function ... generic types are invariant'. The page shows only Function, not Predicate, but 'generic types are invariant' is stated generally.

recorded.prompt:q-boxing-many-steps:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-boxing-many-steps:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-boxing-many-steps:b: Refuted by the one-lambda run: ten million i, 28 KB, 'the JIT inlined it, saw that no `Integer` escaped, and removed the boxing', so values above the cache are not boxed on every call by themselves. Partly true: the conclusion (two Integers per call) is right, and the cache range is part of why the megamorphic case allocates ('the `Integer` cache covers only -128 to 127'); the error is naming the cache as the cause.
